Candidate-set CE uses \(z_i=s_i/\tau\), \(L=-z_++\operatorname{logsumexp}(z_+,\{z_j\}_{j\in S})\): competition within the sampled candidates, without proposal correction. Wu et al.’s [equations and temperature analysis](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.02327) cover this objective under “sampled softmax”; terminology alone does not establish correction. Smaller temperature emphasizes hard negatives; tune it on validation. Mask padding positions and duplicate-negative logits before logsumexp.

Sampling-corrected softmax instead uses \(z_i-\log Q_i\), where \(Q_i\) must match the sampler’s expected counts/inclusion probabilities ([TensorFlow equations](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf)). A common uniform correction cancels only when applied equally to every candidate. Here the positive is inserted deterministically and excluded from sampling: do not evaluate its zero negative-proposal probability. Derived importance-partition alternative: \(\hat Z=e^{z_+}+\sum_{j\in S}e^{z_j}/\pi_j\), targeting \(\{+\}\cup A_u\), with eligible negatives \(A_u\). For 64 replacement draws followed by deduplication, \(\pi_j=1-(1-1/|A_u|)^{64}\); for 64 unique draws, \(\pi_j=64/|A_u|\). Deduplication therefore changes correction; it also leaves fewer than 64 negatives unless refilled. Use stable logsumexp; log of an unbiased partition estimate remains biased. [Sampler documentation](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/random/uniform_candidate_sampler) distinguishes replacement and post-rejection probabilities.

[gSASRec’s official implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch/main/train_gsasrec.py) implements \(L=[\beta\,\mathrm{softplus}(-s_+)+\sum_j\mathrm{softplus}(s_j)]/(k+1)\), \(\beta=1-t+t\alpha\), \(\alpha=k/(|I|-1)\). Calibration parameter \(t\) is not temperature: zero gives BCE; one gives the paper’s calibrated setting under its assumptions. Direct weighted softplus avoids its positive-logit transformation. User-conditioned exclusions and deduplication change those sampling assumptions. Training-positive exclusion removes known false negatives; unseen items remain uncertain. No held-out interactions are needed or justified. gSASRec evidence supports gBCE, not corrected softmax.
